title: SVG Joint Proxy Transform Wrapper

text: Exit animations must never mirror enter amplitude. Because viewer attention moves ahead to the next scene, exit tweens should use 40-60% smaller travel distance and faster duration than enters (e.g., enter: translateY 20px -> 0 over 400ms; exit: translateY 0 -> -8px over 250ms with 4px blur). Symmetrical exits distract from incoming focal subjects.

title: Text Reading Hold Duration Formula
text: Calculate required static hold durations for kinetic titles, cards, and text overlays using `duration = (word_count * 0.3s) + 0.5s` settle time. At 30 fps, a 3-word title needs at least 1.4s (42 frames) hold before transition or exit. Prevents visual cards and sentence highlights from disappearing before viewers can read them.

title: Narrative Arc Echo Rule (Setup-Turn-Echo)
text: Every 30–60 s explainer script must follow a strict three-phase spine: one subject with one goal, exactly one pivotal turn, and an echo ending. title: Cross-Scene J-Cut and L-Cut Sound Transitions

title: Small-Speaker Harmonic Bass Mastering
text: Mobile phone speakers cannot reproduce sub-bass (20–120 Hz), causing synth bass to disappear or distort. Balance low-end energy by keeping 20–120 Hz at −3 dB relative to mids, omit chord and pad notes below MIDI note 48 (C3), and enrich basslines with 2nd and 3rd harmonics so mobile speakers clearly project perceived pitch.

title: Spelled-Out TTS with Digitized Captions
text: TTS engines frequently misread or inconsistently vocalize raw numbers, acronyms, and dates, whereas viewers process digits 3x faster than written words. Always generate two parallel streams: spell numbers phonetically in the spoken script for TTS (e.g., 'ten thousand dollars', 'nineteen eighty four'), but encode them as digits ('$10,000', '1984') in the on-screen captions.

title: FFmpeg Post-Render Grain Injection
text: Rendering film grain dynamically in HTML/Canvas causes every browser screenshot to be noisy and incompressible, drastically slowing headless capture. Instead, render clean frames in headless Chrome and inject procedural grain during the FFmpeg muxing pass (`-vf noise=alls=...:allf=t`). When encoding grain, pass `-tune grain` with an adjusted CRF to preserve texture without macroblocking.

title: Google Fonts Query-Text Dynamic Subsetting

Query Google Fonts CSS API using `&text=<URL_ENCODED_CHARACTERS>` containing only the unique glyphs appearing in the script. Download the resulting ultra-compact WOFF2/TTF (<50 KB) locally and load via `@font-face`.

title: AAC Inter-Sample Peak Stepback Loop
text: Lossy AAC encoding frequently creates inter-sample true-peak overshoots even when the source WAV is limited to -1.2 dBTP. After muxing, measure the audio stream with ebur128. If true peak exceeds -1.0 dBTP, re-encode only the audio track (-c:v copy) with a progressively lower limiter ceiling (stepping down 0.4 dB) up to 3 times until true peak <= -1.0 dBTP.

Launch Chromium with the ANGLE backend set explicitly to SwiftShader (--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader or LEMO_ANGLE=swiftshader) in server/CI environments to guarantee deterministic software rasterization without requiring physical GPU pass-through.

Any match immediately fails preflight and triggers scene regeneration, preventing raw brace syntax from ever reaching rendered video frames.

title: Clean Still Frame Heuristic Auditor

Sample 4 fps downscaled raw frames (160x90 gray), compute median luminance mean, standard deviation, inter-frame diff (near-cut), and spatial gradient. Reject frames where mean < 0.35*m_mean, mean > m_mean+0.25, std < 0.3*m_std, cut_diff > 3.5*m_cut, or gradient < 0.4*m_grad. Step up to ±10 frames (2.5s) to find the nearest clean frame.

Derive an emulsion mask by detecting outer scanner white borders touching boundaries, ensuring broken glass corners and border chips transmit pure 0.97 cool table backlight without emulsion.

title: True-Area Geometric Quantity Scaling Rule

Discs must scale radius by sqrt(factor) to preserve true visual area equivalence. Use area-based scaling whenever comparing tech metrics, cost, or market sizes in lab explainers.

title: Local-Light Modulated Volumetric Fog
text: Uniform scene fog lifts deep shadows into flat gray washed-out rectangles, destroying silhouette contrast in dark corridors. Multiply fog color by local surface illumination relative to average light: `fog_color * clamp(local_bounce / avg_bounce, 0.0, 1.0)`. Where scene lights are dead or off, fog density darkens to near-zero, rendering distant figures as true silhouette voids ('holes in the light').

how: Modify 'mix.py' to detect 'turn' moments in the script. Insert a 0.5s-0.8s hard mute on the music/ambience tracks while keeping a single high-frequency SFX cue (like a terminal beep).

title: Boustrophedon Coloring Path
text: Reveal color blocks using a back-and-forth 'zigzag' path rather than a simple fade or wipe. This mimics the physical act of coloring with a marker or stylus, making the automation feel more 'human' and hand-drawn.
how: In 'ipad-sketch' style videos, apply a 'clip-path' animation to color blocks that follows a serpentine SVG path instead of a linear left-to-right mask.

title: Isometric Assembly Engine
text: True orthographic 45° projection (azimuth 45°, elevation 35.264°) where three axes meet at 120°. Uses a state table to track parts (added/fitted/white). Objects are drawn as line art with flat fills and no perspective distortion.
how: Create 'compose_manual.py' using a new 'iso.js' module for HyperFrames. Implement the 120° axis mapping to render tech hardware (chips, phones) as assembly steps instead of just 2D UI panels.

title: Wet-Bleed Ink Compositor
text: A multi-layer rendering approach for 'Ink Wash' styles. Layer 1: Wet bleed using a 12-tap noisy Poisson blur (5px) with edge pigment accumulation. Layer 2: Dry 'flying white' strokes showing paper texture. Tone logic: 5 specific opacities from 16% (clear) to 96% (burnt).
how: Integrate into 'Puraan Ki Katha' pipeline. Add a Cloudflare FLUX post-processing pass or a CSS filter stack in HyperFrames that simulates ink spreading on paper-textured backgrounds.

title: Parts Explosion Logic
text: Automated 'unboxing' where components fly from a central container along dotted guide lines to a sorted list. Each part eases in and has a small 'settle' bounce. Parts are sorted by view depth to prevent interlock clipping.
how: Build a 'explode.js' utility for HyperFrames. Use it in tech explainers to break down a complex topic into its 10 scored ideas (from ideas.py) visually at the start of the video.

title: Nested Cutaway Dive Timing
text: A three-push sequence through nested cutaways using 'slow → faster → fastest' timing (0.9s, 0.6s, 0.6s) to simulate a fall. Audio low-pass closes further at each level.
how: Add a 'dive' transition preset to plan.py. In mix.py, automate a frequency cutoff sweep that matches these three timing intervals during scale transitions.

title: Hinged Lid-Off Reveal
text: Revealing interiors by flipping the roof/wall on its far hinge like a paper flap (0.35s ease-out) before it glides away. The underside is a neutral paper color.
how: In our layout engine, add a 'hinge' property to top-level containers. Animate the rotation around the far edge axis to reveal internal 'lab' components.

title: Three-Tone Normal Shading Formula
text: Generate 3 tones from one base hex: Top (+20% warm white), Left (+y face, base color), Right (+x face, +22% cool dark like #231A2C).
how: Update our color utility to automatically generate this specific 3-tone palette for all isometric blocks, ensuring consistent lighting without a real 3D light source.

title: Log-Interpolated Zoom
text: Camera zoom uses log-interpolation (px per unit) to handle extreme scale changes smoothly, e.g., from a single bean (k=8000) to a whole board (k=3.75).
how: Modify the camera controller in our rendering engine to use logarithmic scaling for zoom transitions, allowing seamless 'Powers of Ten' style dives between micro and macro assets.

title: Isotype Silhouette Generation
text: Representing quantities by arranging identical icons into meaningful silhouettes (e.g., 70 bean icons forming the shape of a coffee cup). Icons pop with a back-ease overshoot.
how: Create a utility to arrange small SVG/PNG assets into grid-based silhouettes defined by a mask. Use GSAP to stagger their entrance with a 2.2 overshoot ease.

title: Focus + Context Desaturation
text: At the emotional peak or key fact, desaturate everything in the scene toward warm grey except the subject, which keeps its unique hue.
how: Implement a 'desat' property in our render queue. Apply a grayscale CSS filter to the background container while exempting the 'tracked' object ID.

title: Automated Motion/Collision Audit
text: A pre-render check that reports jumps, stop-start stepping, or objects/people standing closer than a defined threshold (e.g., 0.35m).
how: Add a coordinate-tracking loop in preflight.py that analyzes the position data of all simulated entities across frames to flag collisions or velocity spikes.

title: Intellectual Montage (A + B → C)
text: Collision editing where two shots create a new concept. Example: A document's heading ('The Men') + footage of workers → the idea that the document ignores the real labor. Pacing accelerates by halving shot lengths (0.5s -> 0.25s -> 0.125s).
how: Update `plan.py` to identify 'Collision' scenes where two contrasting visuals are paired to prove a point, rather than just illustrating the script.

title: Structural Type Axis
text: Locking all text to a fixed diagonal axis (e.g., -18°). Type appears on solid bands or blocks, never floating. Bilingual pairs use a CJK block with an English line in Oswald directly underneath.
how: Modify `compose_lab.py` CSS templates to enforce a global rotation variable for all text containers and background 'girder' bands.

title: Primary Source Fact-Check Pattern
text: A strict `FACTS.md` requirement: every claim must be listed with the source URL and the verbatim quoted wording. Arithmetic (e.g., date ranges) must be verified via script.
how: Add a step to `research.py` to output a `claims.json` that `preflight.py` uses to verify on-screen text against the original source text.

title: The Canopy Peel Signature
text: A signature motion move: a horizontal plane descends through a 3D object, removing layers on the beat while a histogram/ruler tracks the height. Perfect for 'revealing' hidden tech or history.
how: Apply this to 'Kaise Tech' videos when explaining internal components (e.g., peeling a CPU or battery layer by layer).

title: Biphonic Audio Alternation
text: Stopping the music entirely for a section to let a real recording (e.g., a rivet gun or machine) drive the cuts, then swelling the music back in for the 'answer' or 'result'.
how: In `mix.py`, implement a 'music gate' that ducks the bed to zero during high-impact foley sequences to increase perceived realism.

title: Percentile-Stretch Print Grade
text: A specific grading function for archive footage: luminance -> percentile stretch (0.7/99.5 for film) -> S-curve (s=0.32) -> map to INK/PAPER hex colors. This ensures archive material looks like a unified two-tone print rather than raw video.
how: Add a grading function to `compose_lab.py` or a new `grade.py` using OpenCV/NumPy to process Muse/archive clips before HyperFrames compositing.

title: U2Net Human Segmentation Cut-outs
text: Using the `u2net_human_seg` model to scissor people from photos, adding a 7px paper-white border. These 'cut-outs' are then stacked into structures (photomontage) rather than just being shown as flat images.
how: Integrate a segmentation step in the image pipeline (after FLUX/Muse) to create transparent PNGs with borders for the 'signature' stacking shots.

title: LiDAR Point Cloud Engine
text: A WebGL-based renderer for Entwine Point Tiles (EPT). Features: height-based color ramps, 'canopy peel' (removing points above a Z-plane), and 'condensation' (points turning into a solid lit surface).
how: Build a new `compose_lidar.py` using a headless browser/Three.js to render USGS or user-provided point clouds for technical explainers.

title: Archive Footage License Auditor
text: A tool to search Internet Archive/Wikimedia Commons, checking for specific license fields (CC0, CC-BY, Public Domain) and verifying 'no copyright notice' for pre-1978 US films.
how: Enhance `scout.py` to use the Internet Archive API to filter for 'Public Domain' and 'CC0' specifically for the 'Katha' and 'Kaise' channels.

title: Panel-as-a-Cut Grammar
text: In manga style, a new panel inking in (0.1s wipe) is the cut. Panels open in reading order (R-to-L for Japan, L-to-R for us). Speed is controlled by the number of panels per beat; calm is one big panel with a slow push.
how: Update plan.py to define 'panels' instead of 'scenes' for the Manga style, using the reading order logic to sequence visual reveals on the beat.

title: The Quiet Panel (Ma) Interval
text: After a major climax or 'shutter hit', use a hard cut to a single wide, quiet panel with no text or effect lines, held through 0.5–1.0s of digital silence. This creates a 'breath' that emphasizes the impact.
how: In plan.py, insert a 'silence_beat' after high-score hook scenes, instructing the renderer to remove all overlays and duck audio to zero.

title: Anisotropic Motion Blur on Whips
text: Apply directional motion blur only during high-speed 'whip-pans' between UI panes. Blur an untransformed wrapper to avoid smearing pixel-art or sharp edges incorrectly.
how: In GSAP transitions, trigger a CSS blur filter on a parent container only when the camera velocity exceeds a specific threshold.

title: Match-Cut Origin Story
text: The video's mascot or hero asset should be 'born' from a UI element already on screen (e.g., a logo block morphing into a character). This creates immediate diegetic continuity.
how: In plan.py, for tech videos, start with the brand logo and animate a specific part of it (like a chip or pixel) into the main actor.

title: DOM-Anchored Actor Placement
text: Mascot or prop positions are derived by measuring the live DOM coordinates of UI elements (buttons, input boxes, list rows) every frame. This ensures the 'actor' always stands perfectly on top of high-resolution, redrawn UI components regardless of layout shifts.
how: In compose_lab.py, use a 'proxy' system where GSAP targets coordinates from hidden HTML anchor elements, allowing actors to 'ride' UI panels or chat bubbles as they animate.

title: Screentone Thresholding Pipeline
text: Convert generated images into manga-style print. Detail areas (high variance) are hard-thresholded; flat areas (low variance) become a 45° AM dot screen (6–9px cell size). Scale images to display size before screening to prevent moiré/blur.
how: Add a prep_manga.py script using OpenCV/Pillow to apply a threshold and a dot-matrix pattern to FLUX-generated images before they are used in HyperFrames.

title: Time-Lapse Palette Keyframing
text: Define time-of-day as a set of keyframed CSS variables (zenith, horizon, sun_color). Interpolate these over a short duration (2-3s) to simulate a day/night cycle or a 'theme shift' that affects the entire film state.
how: Add a 'theme-warp' function to compose_lab.py that transitions the --accent and --bg-base variables across the timeline.

title: The Dive from Orbit
text: A high-retention opening move: start at a globe view, identify a point with a ring pulse, and push through the atmosphere (dissolve) into a high-detail 3D terrain map. The globe and map cameras must be mathematically aligned to prevent jarring jumps.
how: Apply to Kaise Tech videos involving geography or global tech trends. Update plan.py to specifically request this 'Dive' sequence for location-based hooks.

title: Chroma-Key Manga Asset Prompting
text: Generating 2D assets (pigeons, tech props, characters) in a crisp G-pen manga style with a #00FF00 green screen background. Uses a 'Single Color Accent' rule (e.g., everything B&W except a flat red camera body) for high-contrast visual interest.
how: Update our FLUX/Muse prompting templates for 'lab look' props. Use the 'flat pure red #FF0000' + 'black ink contour' formula to create stylized tech assets for Kaise Tech.

title: Semantic Color Discipline
text: A strict rule for educational content: Blue = Given/Known, Red = Wanted/Unknown/Answer. This color logic must persist from the drawing into the algebra/text overlays so the viewer's eye tracks the logic automatically.
how: Add this to our 'Shared Brain' as a rule for explainers. Ensure plan.py and compose.py coordinate to use these hex codes consistently across labels and diagrams.

title: 3D Terrain Explainer Engine
text: A Three.js system using real elevation (AWS Terrain Tiles) and satellite imagery (Sentinel-2) to create 3D maps. Features vertical exaggeration (x3), baked shadows, and a 'glowing data layer' for routes and pillars. Includes a 'cut the map open' cross-section view showing bathymetry/depth.
how: Integrate into our Three.js stack. Use the provided 'Native Moves' (Dive from Orbit, Flows Converge) as standard scene templates in plan.py. Fetch tiles via a new fetch_tiles.py utility.

title: Seasonal Wave Transition
text: A 3D transition where a 'wave' spreads from a central point (e.g., a tree), swapping material properties (colors, patterns) as it passes. Objects can 'squat and spring' or 'pop up' as the radius reaches their coordinates.
how: Implement in our Three.js/Diorama scenes. Use a shader that compares pixel distance from a center point to a 'radius' uniform to toggle between two material states.

title: Acceleration Speed Ladder
text: A retention technique where five elements accelerate together: BPM, scene length, stage dwell time, text hold duration, and animation frame rate (e.g., 8fps to 12fps to 24fps). This creates a 'frenzy' effect that builds tension toward a climax.
how: Modify `pace.py` to not just squeeze pauses, but to progressively increase the global 'speed' multiplier and frame-rate target for each subsequent scene in high-energy 'Aage Suno' shorts.

title: Slam-and-Dock Command Hook
text: The hook word/verb 'slams' into the center (overshoot → settle) for <0.5s, then shrinks into a corner tag/badge before the main action starts. This ensures the core hook is delivered without covering the subsequent visual evidence.
how: Apply to `plan.py` for 'Aage Suno'. The first word of the hook should be flagged for 'Slam-and-Dock' treatment in the GSAP timeline instead of standard captions.

title: Procedural Pixel-Color Counting
text: A technique for 'Microscope' style videos where the engine actually counts pixels of a specific color (e.g., blue stain) within a defined ROI and displays the percentage on screen as a rolling counter that 'springs' when it hits the final value.
how: Add a function to `research.py` or a new `analyze.py` that uses OpenCV to mask specific hex ranges in source images, providing real data for 'Kaise Tech' authority-building.

title: Multi-Medium Shader Pipeline
text: A system to render scenes in different artistic 'media' (Crayon, Ink Wash, ASCII, Risograph) using WebGL2 shaders that process pressure, wetness, or plate density channels. The 'jolt' of the style switch acts as a rhythmic beat.
how: Create a `shaders/` directory for `compose.py`. Allow the script to tag scenes with a 'medium' (e.g., `[style: riso]`). Use this for 'Aage Suno' to differentiate story segments.

title: Tuned Foley Synthesis
text: Generating UI SFX (clicks, pings, light-ons) that are tuned to the notes of the current background music's chord or pentatonic scale. This makes the foley feel like part of the score.
how: Modify `mix.py` to accept a 'key' parameter from the music bed and use a simple oscillator to generate UI 'pings' at harmonic frequencies.

title: Strike = Life Rule
text: Use a double-flash 'strike' (100% for 50ms, dark 70ms, 70%, dark, ramp to full) to signify a character waking or a device turning on. It acts as a powerful curiosity trigger in the first 2 seconds.
how: Apply this to 'Kaise Tech' intros. When showing a chip or a new AI tool, have the component 'strike' into life on frame 0 with a transformer hum SFX.

title: 1-2-5 Scale Bar Sequence
text: Scale bars and magnification readouts should follow a 1-2-5 sequence (e.g., 100um, 200um, 500um) and jump only when the magnification changes. This maintains scientific legibility during zooms.
how: Update the 'Lab' look HUD in `compose_lab.py` to snap scale bar values to this sequence based on the current `log_dive` zoom level.

title: Off-Register Cel Jitter
text: Draw fills with a small offset (6px dx, 4px dy) from their ink lines, jittering the offset by ±1.6px on twos (12 fps). This mimics hand-registered 1950s print/animation. Lines should have ±40% width breathing and 15-25% breaks.
how: Add a `shape_toon()` function to our HyperFrames engine that renders a GSAP-animated SVG with a jittered filter or a secondary offset path for the fill layer.

title: Neon Tube Cross-Section Shader
text: Render tubes as concentric bands: gas column (70-85% radius), glass rim, Fresnel edge, and specular streak. Use a Sobel gradient from a profile height map to calculate normals. Gas colors must follow physics (Neon=Red, Argon=Blue).
how: Create a WebGL fragment shader for `compose_lab.py` that takes a polyline and renders the tube profile. Integrate with an emission pyramid for bloom and surface lighting.

title: Limited Animation Pose Rig
text: Animate characters using held body drawings where only arms, hands, eyes, and mouth move. Use 12 fps for poses and hand shapes, but 24 fps for camera and wipes. Hand actions need anticipation, fast action (0.2s), and recoil.
how: Build a `pose.py` module to handle discrete keyframe switching for SVG assets. Update `plan.py` to specify 'pose' tags for specific script beats.

title: Puddle Reflection Engine
text: Mirror the scene facade about the wall base in a 'wet' ground plane. Puddles should be sharp, while wet asphalt is smeared. Reflections must include objects up to two screen heights above the frame to handle low camera angles.
how: In the render pipeline, create a mirrored pass of the scene, apply a ripple/blur shader, and mask it using a noise-generated 'puddle' map.

title: Potential-Flow Route Generator
text: Generate movement paths (e.g., for a robot or character) using streamlines that bend around obstacles and never cross. This ensures 'logical' movement that respects the environment's geometry.
how: Add a `path_logic.py` using potential-flow math to calculate SVG paths for objects moving through 'Lab' look layouts, avoiding UI panels and stat bars.

title: Frosted Glass Panel UI
text: Use dark translucent glass (rgba(12,14,17,0.74)) over a blurred copy of the frame for subtitles and readings. This ensures white text remains readable over both light and dark backgrounds without switching colors.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` to use `backdrop-filter: blur()` for all UI panels and caption boxes, replacing simple semi-transparent backgrounds.

title: Bilingual Non-Wrap Rule
text: Every label/caption is bilingual (Hinglish/English) on exactly one line each; never wrap text. If it's too long, shorten the wording, don't wrap.
how: Add a length-check to preflight.py that flags any bilingual caption exceeding the safe-zone width before rendering.

title: 120/200 BPM Rhythmic Grid
text: All cuts, slams, and label entrances must land on a beat or half-beat of a 120 (News) or 200 (Newsreel) BPM grid.
how: Update plan.py to align scene durations to multiples of 0.5s (for 120 BPM) or 0.3s (for 200 BPM).

title: Sting-to-Bug Continuity
text: The intro sting (logo animation) does not end; its main brand plate flies to the top-right corner to become the channel bug for the rest of the video.
how: In compose_lab.py, animate the intro logo's final transform to the corner bug coordinates (x: 1739, y: 86) instead of a hard cut to the scene.

title: Proportional Spec Card
text: A layout showing 'the whole vs. the part' on a single scale (e.g., 816B total vs 42B active parameters) using proportional bars and a percentage badge.
how: Create a spec_card.js component in HyperFrames that takes two values and renders them as overlapping or adjacent bars on a shared axis for Kaise Tech.

title: Threshold Break Logic
text: A line chart advances one step per beat; when it crosses a defined 'threshold' (e.g., -20% bear market), it triggers a screen shake, impact ring, and a heavy SFX hit.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a 'limit' parameter to charts. When the data point exceeds the limit, trigger a GSAP shake and a timpani SFX event.

title: Strap-Tab Category System
text: The lower-third strap includes a small 'category tab' (e.g., TECH, POLICY, MYTH) that flashes white when the category changes between stories.
how: Modify the caption layer in compose.py to include a persistent tab element that updates its text and flashes opacity on scene transitions.

title: Grease-Pencil Detail Highlight
text: Freeze the frame on a specific detail, apply a jolt/shake, and draw a hand-drawn SVG circle or arrow (grease-pencil style) around the evidence.
how: Add a pencil_highlight.js effect to HyperFrames that renders a 'drawn' SVG path over a static frame at a specific timestamp.

title: Map Document Fly-out
text: On a map, documents (RFI letters/contracts) fly out from a specific city coordinate to their destination on an arc (0.5s) with typewriter SFX.
how: In the map component, use a screen-space projection to link document assets to geographic coordinates, animating them along a Bezier path.

title: Spinning Paper Transition
text: A newspaper/document spins 2.5 turns into the lens, slams with a damped sine bounce (16px), then pushes into the headline.
how: Create a spin_slam.js transition in HyperFrames using GSAP rotation and a custom 'bounce' ease for the final scale-up.

title: Split-Screen Audio Gating
text: In a split-screen 'duel', pan the audio for each side (Left/Right) and gate the music so it trades bars or beats between channels.
how: Update mix.py to support channel-specific volume automation based on which side of a split-screen is 'active' or highlighted.

title: Diegetic-Only Typography
text: Eliminate overlay captions in favor of text written directly on 3D props (stencils on crates, labels on buttons, logs on desks). Text must be bold enough to survive the render grid (Latin cap height ≥ 9px internal). This forces the audience to look at the 'world' of the video rather than reading a UI layer.
how: In `plan.py`, instruct Gemini to place key facts on specific props (e.g., 'The date is stamped on a folder') instead of as a caption. In `compose_lab.py`, map text textures onto 3D primitive surfaces.

title: Object-Anchored Bayer Dither
text: A 3D rendering technique where a 1-bit (black/white) Bayer dither pattern is fixed to object-space coordinates rather than screen-space. This prevents the 'swimming' effect during camera moves. It uses depth and normal breaks to draw 1px outlines, ensuring objects remain visible against same-colored backgrounds (e.g., a black ship against a black sky gets a white rim).
how: Update `compose_lab.py` to include a dither shader pass. Modify the G-buffer to export object-space positions and use them to sample a threshold texture, ensuring the dot pattern 'rides' with our 3D props during Ken Burns or rotation moves.

title: Nib-Follow Camera Logic
text: A camera tracking system that follows a moving point (like a pen nib or a data line) with a specific 'follow weight.' It uses a weighted average of the point's position (e.g., -0.5s to +0.4s) to create natural-looking lag and anticipation, keeping the subject within a 70% safe zone.
how: Add a `follow_point` parameter to our GSAP camera rig. Instead of hard-locking to an object, use a smoothing function that looks ahead at the next 10 frames of the path to 'anticipate' turns, making our 'flow' and 'chart' animations feel more cinematic.

title: Logarithmic Knob Zoom Logic
text: When zooming into technical details (like a graph corner), use logarithmic scaling. As the zoom increases, the graticule (grid) must refine, fading in a finer level of subdivisions (e.g., levels of 5). Readouts for 'TIME/DIV' or 'V/DIV' must update live to match the current zoom level, maintaining mathematical accuracy.
how: Modify 'compose_lab.py' to link the 'zoom' variable to the opacity of a secondary CSS grid and a dynamic text readout that calculates scale based on the zoom factor.

title: Biphonic Event Sonification
text: Sync audio ticks to visual 'corners' or 'marks'. For technical styles, use relay clacks for 'STOP/RUN' events and knob detent clicks for zoom changes. For drawing styles, synthesize paper-friction noise (band-passed noise) where the volume and pitch are proportional to the nib's current screen speed.
how: In 'mix.py', ingest the velocity data from the render engine to modulate a noise generator or trigger specific SFX samples (clicks/ticks) at high-curvature timestamps.

title: Computed Readout Verification
text: Every number shown on screen (measurements, percentages, coordinates) must be computed from the same variables that drive the animation. Never hard-code text values for data. This ensures that if the animation timing or scale changes, the data remains 'factually' consistent with the visual.
how: Update 'research.py' to output raw data. In 'compose_lab.py', use JS to calculate and display these values dynamically within the HTML template rather than using static labels.

title: Speed-Based Pen Pressure Simulation
text: Vary line width dynamically based on drawing speed using the formula: Width = base_width × (0.66 + 0.8·exp(−v/300)). Fast movements result in thinner lines, while slow movements create fatter, weighted lines. This mimics real ink behavior where the nib deposits more material when lingering.
how: In 'compose_lab.py', instead of a constant stroke-width, use a custom GSAP plugin or an SVG filter that modulates 'stroke-width' based on the current velocity of the drawing head.

title: Epicycle Chain Engine
text: A system for drawing complex curves using a chain of rotating circles (Fourier series). Each circle's radius and frequency are defined by the math, and the 'tip' of the final circle draws the path. Includes 'afterglow'—ghosts of the path from previous frames that fade over time.
how: Create a new component in 'HyperFrames' that takes an array of frequencies/amplitudes and uses GSAP to animate the nested rotation of SVG groups.

title: 12/24 FPS Hybrid Sampling
text: Sample character poses at 12 fps (hard steps) while keeping camera, lights, and environment at 24/60 fps. This 'Limited Animation' style provides a tactile, handmade feel (like paper-cut or stop-motion) without sacrificing the smoothness of the cinematic macro camera moves.
how: Apply a `floor(t * 12) / 12` quantization to character transform functions in `layout.js` while leaving the camera `track` function unquantized.

title: Macro Scale Mismatch Rule
text: Combine photoreal 3D environments (wood desk, real lamp) with highly stylized flat actors (cut-paper with white borders). The mismatch in scale—flat 3cm actors under a real macro lens with shallow DOF (aperture 2.2–2.5)—creates a 'tiny world' effect that feels more premium than pure 2D or pure 3D.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` to place our UI panels and props on a high-res walnut or metallic surface with Three.js DOF enabled, rather than a flat black background.

title: Inset Contour Rule
text: For flat-on-flat overlaps (e.g., a red arm over a red body), use an 'inset contour'—a thin slit or line 1.5–3.5 units inside the outline. This separates shapes of the same color without needing artificial shadows or different hues, maintaining the 'paper-cut' aesthetic.
how: Add to the image generation prompt in Muse/FLUX: 'flat papercut style with internal inset contour lines for depth'.

title: Fold-Cut-Unfold Climax Logic
text: A visual metaphor where a sheet is folded 2/4/8 times, a single pattern is cut, and then unfolded to reveal a complex symmetric result (e.g., 8 lanterns from one cut). Use `cos(theta)` compression and 1.28x height enlargement on flaps to simulate 3D folding in a 2D plane, with a 'pa!' snap (ease-out) on the final reveal.
how: Build as a new transition module for `Puraan Ki Katha`. Use it to reveal complex mythological symbols or crowds from a single 'seed' character.

title: Contours Growing Outward
text: For terrain or data reveals, plot levels from the center/summit outward. Use nearest-neighbor ordering for the path and trigger one 'jump' (time-lapse step) per beat. This creates an organic growth effect for maps and heatmaps that feels more structured than a simple fade.
how: In `research.py` or a new `data_viz.py`, process DEM/CSV data into concentric rings of polylines for the plotter engine to draw.

title: Biphonic Character Blips
text: Replace TTS for secondary characters or 'UI feedback' with waveform blips: square waves at C6 for 'hero' feedback, 180–240 Hz triangle waves for 'grumpy' or 'heavy' feedback. Trigger one blip every second character typed in a speech bubble.
how: Add to `mix.py`. When a script has 'chat bubbles', generate these synth blips automatically based on character count to save on TTS credits and add style.

title: Chapter-Hue Color Discipline
text: Assign exactly one hue per 'chapter' or segment of the video. Use a palette of five tones (t0 darkest to t4 lightest) of that specific hue for all elements in that segment.
how: Update `plan.py` to assign a 'Segment Hue' to each scene group. Modify `compose_lab.py` to map its UI panels, charts, and accents to the tones of the assigned hue.

title: One Verb Per Item Rule
text: Every featured object or prop in a scene must perform exactly one clear, readable action per beat or bar (e.g., the umbrella opens, then furls, then turns). Avoid static or aimless motion.
how: In the `plan.py` prompt, instruct Gemini to assign a specific 'Action Verb' to every primary prop mentioned. The motion engine then executes only that specific transformation.

title: System-as-Metaphor Narration
text: Use game or simulation mechanics to express abstract concepts: 'Save Files' for memories, 'Level Up' for growth, or 'Greyed Out' UI elements for loss or unavailability.
how: In `plan.py`, tell Gemini to use 'Game UI Metaphors' for 'Aage Suno' stories. For example, a character's failure is shown as a 'Game Over' screen or a depleted HP bar.

title: Protected Color Anchor
text: Exempt one specific color index (e.g., a brand red) from all palette effects, fades, or chapter-hue shifts. This color remains constant as a visual thread throughout the film.
how: Define a `BRAND_ACCENT` hex in `compose.py`. Ensure the CSS filter logic for 'fading' or 'hue-shifting' excludes any element tagged with the `.protected-color` class.

title: The Morning Wave Transition
text: A diagonal accent-colored band sweeps the frame; new elements/data pop up behind the wave, while old elements sink ahead of it. Useful for showing evolution or 'before/after' states.
how: Create a `sweep_reveal.js` component in HyperFrames. Use it in 'Kaise Tech' videos when transitioning from an old technology version to a new one.

title: Integer-Pixel Motion Quantization
text: Round all camera and parallax offsets to the nearest integer pixel. This prevents sub-pixel shimmering and maintains the 'pixel-perfect' clarity of UI and text elements.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, wrap GSAP animation updates in a function that applies `Math.round()` to the `x` and `y` coordinates of all moving panels and props.

title: The Dot-Pull Reveal
text: Start the video at 20x zoom inside a textured area where Ben-Day dots are massive (coin-sized). Pull back logarithmically to reveal the full subject. This establishes the 'printed' medium and creates immediate scale curiosity.
how: In `plan.py`, for Pop Art styles, force the first scene to start at `scale: 20` on a high-contrast area, using a 1.5s exponential ease-out to `scale: 1`.

title: Own-Color Outline Rule
text: Instead of black outlines, ring every part in a darker shade of its own fill color (e.g., Color * 0.52). This creates a 'soft cel' look common in technical anatomy plates and prevents the 'comic book' feel.
how: Modify `compose_lab.py` to calculate the `stroke` color dynamically based on the `fill` color of SVG elements, rather than using a hardcoded black or neutral outline.

title: Mosaic Echo Ending
text: A final camera pull-out where the individual 'tiles' or 'prints' from the video shrink to become single pixels of a much larger hero image, with a heavy key line drawn along the edges of the tiles.
how: In `compose.py`, create an end-card template that takes the last 10 frames, treats them as a grid, and overlays a high-contrast 'hero' silhouette whose colors are derived from the average tile colors.

title: RPG Dialog Box Grammar
text: Place subtitles in a dedicated dark-blue dithered box at the bottom quarter. Include a 32x32 pixel portrait of the 'speaker' (e.g., an AI icon or historical figure) on the left. Text types at 40 chars/s.
how: Create a new caption preset in `compose.py` called 'RPG_BOX'. Use a pixel-style font and a GSAP 'TextPlugin' to simulate the typing, paired with the 'Text Blips' audio build.

title: Plate-by-Plate Stamping
text: A transition where an image is assembled by its color plates (Yellow, Red, Blue, then Black Key) landing sequentially with a physical 'thunk' sound. Each plate should be slightly misregistered (1-2px offset) to simulate physical printing.
how: In `compose.py`, create a 'PrintStamp' transition that renders the asset four times with different CSS `mix-blend-mode` filters, staggering their entry by 0.1s and adding a random `translate` offset.

title: World-Space Section Hatching
text: Procedural 45-degree hatching applied to 'cut' faces of a 3D or 2D object. The hatching must be computed in world units so it remains stable and does not 'swim' or jitter when the camera moves or orbits.
how: Add a 'Hatch' material to `compose_lab.py`. Use a CSS `linear-gradient` pattern with `background-attachment: local` (or a fixed SVG pattern) on clipped elements to ensure the texture moves with the object.

title: Exploded-View Axis Logic
text: An animation state where components of a system lift apart along a central axis to show internal layers. Removing one layer (e.g., a 'governor') should trigger a visual change in the remaining parts (e.g., gears spinning faster).
how: In `compose_lab.py`, implement an 'explode' function that applies staggered Y-axis translations to a group of elements based on their 'layer' attribute, synced with a 'speed' variable in the physics engine.

title: Plate-Layered Arrangement Orchestration
text: Tie musical instrumentation strictly to visual visual layer introduction. Start with a single acoustic instrument (e.g. nylon guitar or bass) during monochrome/single-element visuals. Introduce rhythm (percussion/shaker) when the second color/visual plane arrives, harmonic melody when the third arrives, and full ensemble at peak overprint/climax. Drop all instruments on tension holds except environmental foley, snapping back fully on downbeat.
how: Apply in `plan.py` scene audio prompts and `mix.py` procedural stem builder to correlate asset entrances with music track stem activation.

title: BPM-Locked Harmonized Prop Breathing
text: Make all idle visual props, containers, and background cards breathe in phase with narration tempo using `cos(2π·beats)`: stretch along Y on the beat (~1.05×) and squash on the off-beat (~0.95×), stepped on twos (12 fps) while camera translates on ones (24/30 fps). At narrative payoff peaks, scale breathing amplitude ×3 to bounce the entire layout.
how: Add an idle breathing ticker in HyperFrames (`compose_lab.py`) synced to the audio track's detected BPM from `mix.py`, applying stepped affine scaling to active props.

title: Reaction Close-Up Rule
text: In dialogue-driven or absurd content, every reveal of an absurd image or 'wrong' result must be followed immediately by a reaction close-up of the character. The comedy/impact lives on the face, not just the object.
how: Add a rule to plan.py: if a scene contains a 'reveal' or 'absurd fact', the following scene must be a 1.5s close-up reaction shot.

title: Hatching as Gradient
text: Instead of digital gradients, use dense zigzag hatching that overshoots outlines to create light/shadow. Large light sources are achieved by stacking sparse hatch layers.
how: In Puraan Ki Katha (mythology), use SVG pattern fills with diagonal lines instead of CSS gradients to create a more 'hand-crafted' or 'ancient' look.

title: Georeferenced Plate Nesting Engine
text: A shader-based system that samples georeferenced imagery (Landsat/Blue Marble) nested by resolution (world -> region -> detail) with feathered edges. It allows for a continuous logarithmic zoom from orbit to ground level without resolution jumps.
how: Update compose_lab.py to include a WebGL2 layer that handles lon/lat coordinate mapping for imagery plates, replacing static photos with nested textures for tech explainers.

title: Line-by-Line FACTS.md Audit
text: A verification workflow where every number, year, and claim in the script is mapped to a specific source URL and exact wording in a FACTS.md file. A pre-render check ensures no number exists in the video that isn't in the table.
how: Integrate into preflight.py; have Gemini extract all numbers from the script and match them against a provided research doc before allowing the render to start.

title: Scratch-In Reveal Engine
text: A motion effect where lines or characters are drawn live behind a 'hot point' (a white core with flying chips). The line appears progressively as if scratched into emulsion, with a thin overshoot tail.
how: Create a new GSAP preset in HyperFrames that uses drawSVG but adds a 'spark' element (a small div with a glow) that follows the path's leading edge.

title: Range Line with Rolling Counter
text: A measurement tool that grows a ticked line from Point A to Point B while a reticle at the tip displays a rolling numerical readout (e.g., '95 km') that lands exactly when the line stops.
how: Build a reusable GSAP component that syncs a 'km' counter's innerText to the percentage completion of a line's drawSVG progress.

title: Lip-Sync Envelope Mapping
text: Extracting RMS (volume/openness) and spectral centroid (width/roundness) from TTS audio at 24Hz to drive parametric mouth shapes (open, width, curl) at 12fps.
how: Add a step after TTS generation to export a JSON of volume peaks per frame; use this to drive the 'scaleY' of mouth SVGs in HyperFrames.

title: Carving-as-Density Texture Logic
text: Create complex 'lace' patterns by treating alpha as material density. Use destination-out/destination-in operations in Canvas to cut patterns (crescents, lattices, coin holes) into a base texture while maintaining a dark 2px 'ink' outline on all edges.
how: Apply to Puraan Ki Katha for 'mandir' architecture or character clothing. Use procedural SVG masks to 'carve' details into our FLUX-generated assets.

title: Abduction-First Arm Rigging
text: Rigging rule: Apply abduction (outward swing) before flexion (forward swing). This prevents arms from crossing and obscuring the face during 'raised arm' poses. Includes clavicle rise (shoulder joint moving up) as the arm elevates.
how: Update our mathematical character rigging logic. Ensure the 'shoulder' pivot is dynamic rather than fixed to the torso corner.

title: Percussion-First Rhythmic Scoring
text: Score structure based on 'Gong-and-Drum' patterns (锣鼓经). Map specific hits (big gong for reveals, small gong for decisions, accelerating rolls for entrances) to visual beats. Hard-cut the audio bed (≤30ms) for 'silent choice' moments.
how: Update mix.py to accept 'hit' events from the timeline. Use a library of traditional percussion samples instead of generic music beds for high-impact mythology scenes.

title: Dual-Energy Colorizer Shader
text: A full-screen shader that maps material classes to specific hues: Organic (Zeff < 10) = Orange, Mixed (10-18) = Green, Metal (> 18) = Blue. Brightness is determined by total attenuation, peaking then falling to black for impenetrable objects.
how: Add a WebGL post-processing fragment shader to our render pipeline. Map our 3D prop metadata (material tags) to these specific RGB channels before the colorizer pass.

title: Scan-Line Sweep Transition
text: A transition where the incoming frame is revealed behind a moving vertical line (right-to-left, matching belt flow). The outgoing frame is frozen and held to the left of the line. Duration: 0.2s for montages, 0.5s for scene shifts.
how: Update compose.py to include a 'sweep' transition type. It requires rendering the last frame of the previous scene as a static texture to be wiped.

title: Pendulum/Spring Chain Simulation
text: Secondary motion for loose parts (tassels, hair, limbs) driven by parent body acceleration. Pre-simulated at a high rate (120Hz) for determinism, then sampled at the film's frame rate. Adds organic 'tremor' and weight.
how: Integrate a simple Verlet or spring-chain solver into our GSAP-based HyperFrames. Apply to character rigs in mythology stories to make jewelry and hair react to movement.

title: World-to-Film Iris Tracking
text: An iris-wipe effect where the center tracks a specific subject (e.g., a face) even during camera zooms or pans. Requires mapping world-space coordinates to normalized film-space coordinates after all transforms.
how: Add an 'iris_focus' target to plan.py. The render engine will calculate the center point per frame based on the subject's position in the final viewport.

title: Registration Offset Logic
text: Apply a 1-3px random offset (registration slip) to different visual layers (e.g., text, icons, background). This creates 'paper-white' slivers where layers don't perfectly align, adding a physical, analog quality to automated digital renders.
how: In compose.py, add a small random 'top/left' jitter to absolute-positioned elements within a scene, specifically between the 'highlight box' and the 'caption text'.

title: The 'Freeze-Orbit' Signature
text: On a key beat (the climax or hook), freeze all subject motion (droplets, characters, physics) while the camera continues to move (orbit or zoom) and the background environment (sky colors) continues to shift. This emphasizes a 'moment that matters'.
how: Implement a 'Global Pause' in the HyperFrames timeline that excludes the camera-wrapper and background-shader elements. Trigger this via a 'climax' tag in the scene plan.

title: Silhouette-on-Light Rule
text: Silhouettes must always sit on a light source (sun, horizon, water glitter), never on a dark background. If a subject is in a dark zone, it must be moved into a 'glitter column' or highlighted by a volumetric rim light to remain readable.
how: Add a preflight.py check using Gemini Vision to ensure the primary subject (black silhouette) has sufficient contrast against its immediate background pixels.

title: Formula-Bar Dialogue
text: In tech/data styles, use the formula bar as the primary dialogue delivery mechanism. Type formulas (e.g., =AVERAGE(A:A)) letter-by-letter; the 'Enter' keypress acts as a hard state-cut that triggers a visual change (e.g., a result popping or a chart filling).
how: In plan.py, instruct Gemini to write one 'formula' per scene that summarizes the core fact. Type this into a fixed UI element before the scene's visual climax.

title: Light-Sweep Narrative Clock
text: Use a moving light patch to represent the passage of time or the focus of the story. In a multi-pane layout (like stained glass), only the lit pane moves; others remain frozen. The light 'projects' the story onto the environment (e.g., colored shadows on a floor).
how: In compose.py, use a moving CSS linear-gradient mask to 'activate' different zones of the screen in sequence, synchronized with the script's timeline.

title: Spreadsheet Pixelation Logic
text: Use a spreadsheet grid as the pixel canvas. Cells are wide (2.9:1), and images are formed via conditional formatting rules (e.g., 1=lime, 0=red). The software 'shell' (headers, formula bar) remains fixed while the sheet zooms and scrolls. Values disappear at low zooms to prevent 'grey mush'.
how: Create compose_sheet.py. Render data as a CSS Grid where background-color is driven by cell values. Use the formula bar at the top to display the video's 'dialogue' or key facts.

title: Scissor-Cut Edge Displacement
text: Simulate hand-cut paper by resampling polygon edges every 10px and applying low-frequency noise displacement (1-2px). Cache the edge in local space so it doesn't 'crawl' when the object moves. Add a 2px 'cut gap' (outline in ground color) between overlapping pieces.
how: Apply an SVG filter with feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap to all flat assets in compose.py. Use a small drop shadow with zero blur for paper depth.

title: Diagonal Grid Assembly
text: Split the screen along a 30-degree diagonal. Multiply this into a grid where fragments slide off alternately to reveal a new scene or fly back in to assemble a central title. This creates a high-energy, sophisticated transition for 'Spy' or 'Tech' looks.
how: Create a CSS clip-path utility in layout.js that generates diagonal strips. Use GSAP to stagger the x/y translation of these strips during scene transitions.

title: Swiss Snap-to-Beat Rigor
text: Movement must be exact with zero bounce or overshoot. Use `cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)` for all snaps. Every element arrival must land exactly on a beat or subdivision; deletions use a 2-step 'knife cut' (cross-line then collapse).
how: Add a `swiss` preset to `layout.js`. Enforce the specific bezier curve and disable all spring/elastic easings. Implement the 'knife cut' as a standard GSAP timeline for removing UI elements.

title: Banderole/Parchment Subtitle Logic
text: Subtitles unfurl from the center of a curled parchment banderole. Text only fades in once the ribbon is 75% open. Ribbon must pad significantly past the text width.
how: Add a 'mythology' subtitle style to `Puraan Ki Katha`. Use a 3-part SVG (left-cap, middle-stretch, right-cap) that scales based on Gemini's script line length before the text appears.

title: Extreme Scale Contrast Rule
text: Pair a giant element (e.g., 700px numeral) with tiny technical notes (19px). The giant element acts as a chapter marker/anchor, while the tiny text provides 'texture' and credibility.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` templates to always include a 'micro-spec' corner (bitrate, module size, timestamp) when a large 'hero' stat is displayed.

title: Tangent-Continuous Hose Rig
text: Stick-figure limbs as quadratic curves where joint is the control point. When hands clasp, the two control points are rotated onto a single line through the clasp point to create one continuous 'hose' curve between shoulders.
how: Add to a new `compose_stick.py`. Implement a 2D skeleton where `drawGroup` computes tangent alignment for connected figures, allowing a single stroke to represent multiple joined characters.

title: CAD-to-Video Pipeline
text: Automated extraction of PCB layouts (KiCad) and 3D meshes (STEP) into the render engine. Uses component designations from the Bill of Materials (BOM) to automatically generate labels and leader lines.
how: Build `tools/extract_cad.py` to parse KiCad S-expressions into JSON for `compose_lab.py`. This allows 'Kaise Tech' videos to show real internal circuitry of devices being explained.

title: Accent Run Pulse
text: A liquid-style pulse that flows through connected nodes or joined arms. The stroke length grows over time along the path, filling nodes as it passes. Used to show flow, logic, or connectivity.
how: Implement as a SVG `stroke-dasharray` animation in `HyperFrames`. Use a custom GSAP hook to trigger 'node_fill' events when the dash-offset reaches specific coordinate thresholds.

title: Red-Black Inversion Accent
text: Use 1–6 frame palette swaps (Red <-> Black) for impact beats. Do not use standard RGB inversion (which creates cyan); manually swap the primary and secondary theme colors to maintain brand discipline.
how: Add a `palette_swap` filter to the HyperFrames render pass, triggered by 'impact' cues in the script.

title: Official Rights Chain Verification
text: Strict 4-point check for found footage: 1. Official/Verified channel; 2. CC-BY field present; 3. Native resolution (no AI-upscale); 4. Save JSON evidence of the license field and date checked.
how: Integrate this check into `scout.py`. The 'shared brain' should reject any clip that doesn't meet all four criteria to prevent copyright strikes.

title: Speaker Dialogue Rails
text: A dialogue layout using fixed-color vertical columns (rails) at screen edges. Each character owns a color (e.g., Red/Black). Type is vertical with a small English sub-line. This allows the background to cut rapidly while the dialogue remains persistent and readable.
how: Add `rail()` layout to `compose.py`. Use it for 'Puraan Ki Katha' to handle multi-character dialogue without needing lip-sync or avatars.

title: Overshoot Head-Tilt Rig
text: 2D character animation via layer rotation: Back-turned (-35°) -> 60ms wind-up -> 120ms whip to +0.1 rad with overshoot -> exponential decay settle. Use 3-frame ghosting (28% opacity) during the whip for 'anime' motion blur.
how: Create `rig.py` to split Muse/Flux character outputs into head/body layers. Integrate the 'whip' logic into `compose.py` for story climaxes.

title: Thermal Emissivity Realism Rule
text: Thermal visuals must respect physics: glass and bare metal look cold because they reflect the sky (low emissivity), while brick and skin look warm. Use an 'iron' palette (black-indigo-magenta-orange-yellow-white) where brightness strictly equals temperature. Avoid 'dramatic' coloring; let the heat flow (Gaussians for sources, noise for plumes) drive the glow.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, apply this logic to hardware explainers (e.g., showing a chip heating up). Use FLUX to generate the 'visible' base and a custom CSS filter/shader to simulate the 'iron' palette thermal overlay.

title: Tilt-Shift Time-Lapse Stutter Rule
text: To achieve a 'miniature' look, the world must move in fast, jittery steps (8Hz or 12Hz) while the camera remains smooth. This makes vehicles and people look like wind-up toys. Saturated 'toy-like' colors and a high vantage point (45-55° pitch) are mandatory to trigger the macro-photography illusion.
how: In `compose.py`, implement a 'step-frame' logic for background assets while keeping the GSAP camera movement at 60fps. Increase saturation by 1.5x and contrast by 0.4x for these specific scenes.

title: The 'Speed Drop' Twist
text: Structure the arc to build density in fast-forward (time-lapse), then hard-drop to real-time (x1 speed) on a single human/animal detail for a 'comedy beat' or emotional payoff. Release back to fast-forward for a final scale reveal (e.g., rising to a 'circuit board' view of the city).
how: Apply to 'Aage Suno' stories. Use `plan.py` to identify a 'climax detail' and set the `pace.py` to ramp from high-speed chatter to a silent, real-time pause at that specific timestamp.

title: Diegetic Sensor Simulation
text: Simulate a low-res sensor (320x240 or 640x480) upsampled to 1080p. Add temporal noise, column/row stripes, and corner shading. Instruments like spot meters (crosshairs with values), scale bars, and isotherms (single-color threshold highlights, e.g., green) should be part of the camera HUD, not external graphics.
how: Add a `thermal_hud.js` layer to HyperFrames. Use a coarse pixelation filter on the background and overlay monospace spot meters that 'flicker' their last digit at 6Hz to mimic real sensor refresh rates.

title: Ink-on-Paper Schematic Engine
text: Animate transit lines as if being drawn by a pen tip on paper. Use 'octilinear' bends (45/90 degree angles). Implement an 'interchange impact' where new station capsules fall onto the map with shock rings in the line's color. Use a paper-texture background with ink-bleed shaders.
how: Build `compose_map.py` using SVG paths for lines. Use GSAP `drawSVG` for the pen effect and a 'drop' animation with a scale-up/fade-out ring for interchanges. Apply a subtle grain and paper texture overlay.

title: Jo-Ha-Kyū Narrative Pacing
text: A three-act structure: Jo (slow, still, opening), Ha (gathering pulse/rhythm), and Kyū (rapid rush to peak), followed by 'Ma' (a hard cut to absolute silence/held breath) before a quiet resolution.
how: Update the `plan.py` prompt for Gemini to structure tech/mythology stories using these phases, specifically requesting a 1-second 'Ma' silence before the final 'shock fact' or 'moral'.

title: Mode-Based Line Grammar
text: Distinguishing categories not by color (which is reserved for identity), but by form: Solid (primary), Hollow/Double-Edge (secondary/bus), Dashed (underground/hidden), and Thread-on-Lane (water/ferry).
how: Apply this to tech explainers: use 'hollow' lines for data requests and 'solid' lines for hardware connections, rather than just changing colors which can confuse the palette.

title: Event-Driven Color Arrival Field
text: A visual transition where color 'blooms' or 'spreads' from a source point (like a gust of wind or a character's path) using a ragged wet front and dark tide lines. Objects remain monochrome ink drawings until the 'arrival field' time reaches their coordinates.
how: In HyperFrames, implement a CSS/Canvas mask using a noisy radial gradient that expands over time. Link the `opacity` or `filter: grayscale()` of scene elements to their distance from the 'event' source.

title: Handwritten Margin Colophon
text: Moving text from 'floating overlays' to 'diegetic handwriting'. Titles and credits are written onto the 'paper' margin in a casual hand (Caveat/Reenie Beanie) with left-to-right reveal and pen-scratch audio.
how: For 'Aage Suno' stories, replace standard captions with an SVG path-reveal of a handwriting font in the bottom 'margin' of the frame, synced with the narrator's intro.

title: Copperplate Data Engraving
text: Charts are rendered as 'data engravings' rather than standard plots. Use parallel engraved lines where the stroke width (weight) is modulated by the data value, creating a copperplate swelling-line effect. Include cross-hatching at peaks, thin ochre washes, and double-rule axes. For broken scales, use a physical 'torn break' in the paper rather than a zig-zag line.
how: Update our D3.js integration to output SVG paths with variable stroke-width based on data arrays, or use a custom shader in the HyperFrames pipeline to modulate line thickness by value.

title: Through-the-Hole Transition
text: A diegetic transition where the camera pushes directly into a physical hole or shape in the current scene (e.g., an oval stamp frame, a window, or an empty album slot). The next scene is already 'inside' the hole. This creates a 'rhyme' between scenes and maintains spatial continuity without using generic wipes or fades.
how: In compose.py, define a 'portal' element in Scene A. Use GSAP to scale the entire Scene A container while simultaneously scaling Scene B inside the portal's mask to create a seamless zoom-through.

title: Known vs. Unresolved Columnar Logic
text: For mystery or technical breakdown videos, use a two-column layout to explicitly separate 'Established' facts from 'Unresolved' theories. Use '✓' badges for confirmed items and dashed boxes or '?' for unresolved ones. This builds authority by showing the limits of the research rather than speculating.
how: Add a 'verdict' block to research.py. If Gemini identifies conflicting sources, the script should flag the scene for a 'Two-Column' layout in compose_lab.py.

title: Hard Sync Multi-Source Grid
text: Align multiple independent sources (video, photo, document, audio) to a single 'Hard Sync Point' (e.g., a flash, impact, or gunshot). Sources that start late simply 'light up' or cut in with a white flash at their relative start time on the shared clock. This proves the timeline visually rather than just stating it.
how: Modify plan.py to identify a 'Sync Event'. In compose.py, use a shared 'T+0' timestamp for all assets in a scene, applying individual offsets to their entry frames based on the master event clock.

title: Ransom Letter Eighth-Note Slap
text: Hero words or numbers appear one character at a time as 'ransom letters' (individual paper slips). Each character should have a randomized font (serif/typewriter), paper texture, and rotation. Slap them into the frame at a consistent rhythm, exactly one per eighth note (e.g., 250ms at 120 BPM), accompanied by a physical 'slap' or 'thud' SFX.
how: Create a new HyperFrames component that takes a string and generates a sequence of div-based 'slips' with randomized CSS transforms and font-family, triggered by the BPM-locked timeline.

title: Telegrams on the Clock
text: Display messages (chats, alerts, logs) as physical cards that land at their specific timestamps. Use red dashed 'leader lines' to tie each card to a specific pin on a horizontal or vertical time-axis/data chart. This anchors text-based evidence to a physical timeline.
how: In compose_lab.py, implement a 'Timeline Pin' component that draws a dashed SVG line between a floating text panel and a coordinate on a D3-generated axis.

title: Hand Jitter for Still Assets
text: To avoid the 'static' digital look, apply a subtle, randomized jitter to 'resting' assets (approx 0.7px position and 0.25° rotation) updated every 2-3 frames ('on twos'). The camera moves smoothly, but the assets feel like they are physically placed on a table.
how: Add a 'jitter' loop to the HyperFrames render engine that applies a small Math.random() offset to the transform property of all non-moving elements.

title: The Gradient Walk Structure
text: Map a measurable quantity (rainfall, altitude, time, power) to horizontal distance. The camera move *is* the argument, walking a continuous 'transect' across 4-6 distinct zones with unique palettes and hero specimens.
how: In `plan.py`, instruct Gemini to structure 'Kaise Tech' or 'Katha' scripts as a linear journey along a single axis (e.g., 'Walking through the history of the 4nm chip' or 'Descending through the 7 lokas').

title: The 'Hole' Visual Logic
text: Highlight a specific data set (e.g., 'pre-war buildings' or 'active components') and let the *absence* of light in other areas define the shape of the subject (the 'hole').
how: In `compose_lab.py`, use high-contrast 'emissive' highlights for the subject while dropping the background to near-black, using the lack of detail to draw the eye to the 'missing' or 'unique' parts.

title: Eraser Rewind Transition
text: Use a physical 'eraser' prop to wipe a scene backwards, reading as 'undoing' a mistake or rewinding time. The wiped area leaves a 10% 'ghost' of the previous content.
how: In `plan.py`, use this for 'correction' segments (e.g., 'You might think X... [erase] ...but actually Y'). Implement as a 'destination-out' mask in Canvas.

title: Procedural Painting-In Engine
text: Objects are drawn stroke-by-stroke using a variable-width ribbon + dashed 'bristle tracks' for a 'flying white' dry-brush effect. Progress is a function of screen position or time, drawing structure (trunks) before detail (leaves).
how: Implement in `compose_lab.py` using Canvas2D. Replace static image loads with a `drawList` function that iterates through a points-array, applying a `sin` width profile and partial opacity 'multiply' blending.

title: Projection-on-White-Model Shader
text: Project data/colors onto a matte white 3D model (#F3F3F1). The color is a 'light throw' (dot product of surface normal and projector axis) rather than a texture, allowing layers to 'wash' over geometry.
how: Update our 'CSS 3D Perspective Rig' or Three.js setup to use a custom shader that adds a color term based on a virtual projector position, specifically for hardware (Kaise Tech) or architectural (Katha) models.

title: Peak-to-RMS Look-ahead Limiting
text: For peaky TTS (like Kokoro, ~17dB peak-to-RMS), apply a 5ms look-ahead peak limiter (ceiling = speech RMS + 11dB) *before* level matching to -14 LUFS to prevent clipping while maintaining presence.
how: Update `mix.py` to include a limiting pass using `pydub` or a custom NumPy limiter before the final loudness mastering step.

title: 1/z Zoom Interpolation
text: Interpolate camera zoom in 1/z space rather than linear scale. This makes 'pushes' feel like physical dollies with consistent perceived speed.
how: Update the GSAP camera logic in `layout.js` to use a custom ease or a function that calculates `scale = 1 / (1 + t)` for zoom-ins.

title: Beat-Locked Object Phasing
text: Sync object animations (like hops or pulses) to the music's beat grid. For 'diverging' concepts, run two objects at different tempi (e.g., 120bpm vs 121bpm) until they snap into unison.
how: Use the output of `mix.py` beat detection to drive GSAP 'stagger' or 'repeat' intervals for UI elements or props.

title: Glossy Sheen Drift
text: Add a soft diagonal window sheen (10-16% white) that moves at a different speed (e.g., 0.35x) than the camera. This parallax sheen immediately sells the surface as 'glossy' or 'glass'.
how: Add a semi-transparent gradient overlay in `compose_lab.py` that moves slightly during camera pans.

title: Fact-to-Voice Audit Table

how: Adopt the `FACTS.md` format for the `research.py` output to ensure Hinglish tech explainers are bulletproof before script finalization.

title: Loupe Detail Readout
text: A circular magnifier (loupe) that hovers over a detail, with a leader line connecting to an external high-contrast label. The label stays in screen-space while the loupe follows world-space coordinates.

title: PCB-Routed Font Renderer
text: A monoline font system (font.js/hanzi.js) that draws text using 0/45/90-degree traces with chamfered corners and round caps, mimicking PCB silkscreen.
how: Implement a canvas-based text renderer that uses the provided glyph stroke data to draw text as vector traces, replacing standard web fonts for our 'lab look' titles.

title: Nested Coordinate Level Renderer
text: A hierarchical rendering system (levels.js) that handles infinite zoom/dive transitions by nesting coordinate systems, allowing cameras to move between parent and child boards seamlessly.
how: Integrate the 'toChild' and 'toParent' matrix transformation logic into our HyperFrames pipeline to enable smooth, mathematically precise 'dive from orbit' transitions.

title: Octilinear Routing Engine
text: A geometry utility (geo.js) that forces lines to 45-degree angles (octilinear), essential for creating authentic-looking circuit board traces and technical UI diagrams.
how: Add the 'octi' function to our geometry library to automatically snap UI connection lines and flow charts to 45-degree increments.

title: Octilinear Diagram Routing
text: Using an 'octi' function to constrain paths to 45-degree and 90-degree angles (PCB style). This creates a clean, technical 'lab' look for connecting nodes or drawing geographic features like rivers as copper traces.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` to include an `octilinear_route` helper for flows and UI panels, ensuring all connecting lines snap to 45/90 degree increments for a sharper aesthetic.

title: Geographic-to-PCB Coordinate Mapping
text: Mapping real-world longitude/latitude coordinates to a local PCB coordinate system (1 unit = 1 km) with scaling factors. Allows placing 'cities' as pads and 'rivers' as traces while maintaining spatial accuracy.
how: Apply this in `compose_lab.py` for tech explainers involving maps. Use the `P(lon, lat)` conversion logic to draw accurate but stylized data-viz maps.

title: Procedural Film-Look LUTs
text: Instead of static LUT files, the system generates color grading curves procedurally using numpy (exponential decay for shadows/highlights and specific RGB channel clipping), ensuring consistent 'film' aesthetics across all assets.
how: Replace our current static color correction with a `grade.py` module that uses the provided `make_luts` logic to apply a consistent dark-metallic/sodium-orange look.

title: Hand-Lettering Skeleton Data
text: The `glyphs.json` file maps characters to coordinate skeletons (paths), allowing for procedural handwriting animations that are more authentic than standard font-based 'write-on' effects.
how: Use this data structure to animate our kinetic titles, drawing lines along the skeleton coordinates rather than just masking a font.

title: Reveal-Time Shader Masking
text: Define a 'reveal time' (arev) attribute for every vertex in a mesh. Use a fragment shader to discard pixels where the current time is less than the reveal time, creating a procedural 'draw-in' effect across complex 3D objects.
how: Implement this in our Three.js lab-look renderer to animate the appearance of 3D props (chips, circuit boards) as if they are being sketched in real-time.

title: Automated Puppet Extraction
text: The extract.py tool uses green-screen keying and scipy.ndimage to automatically segment character sheets into individual, pivot-ready parts with consistent margins.
how: Add this to our pipeline to process character sheets generated by FLUX/Muse, automatically creating the parts/ folder and index.json needed for our animation engine.

title: Automated Asset Provenance Tracker
text: A centralized footage manager (footage.py) that fetches assets from archives (NASA, Commons), stores them with metadata (license, source URL, credit), and generates a SOURCES.md file.
how: Add a metadata-tracking layer to our footage-fetching scripts to ensure every asset used is logged with its license and source for compliance.

title: Event-Driven Layout Orchestrator
text: A central events.json file that drives layout changes, HUD updates, and camera swaps, decoupling the visual logic from the rendering loop.
how: Refactor compose.py to ingest an event timeline rather than hard-coding scene transitions, allowing for dynamic multi-cell split-screen layouts.

title: Parametric Character Rigging
text: A system for defining characters (girl, lamb, moon) as fully parametric objects with view, expression, and pose states, allowing for procedural animation without complex skeletal rigs.
how: Adopt this state-based approach for our recurring characters in 'Puraan Ki Katha' to simplify animation logic and ensure visual consistency across different poses.

title: Book-Pullback Transition
text: A technique for transitioning from a full-screen scene into a 3D-simulated book page, including perspective-corrected page turning and gutter shadow rendering.
how: Use the perspective-mapping logic from end.js to create a 'story-book' transition for our 'Puraan Ki Katha' series, pulling out from the story into a book view.

title: Wax-Resist Watercolour Simulation
text: Simulate watercolour washes by using a wax-coverage map to resist pigment, creating tide lines at edges and granulation in deep paper pits.
how: Update our lab look to include a wash-pass shader that uses a coverage map to modulate pigment transmission based on paper-grain depth.

title: Grouped Layer NPR Rendering
text: Organize scene objects into depth layers (bg, ch, fg) with distinct crayon rendering styles per layer. Apply randomized stroke parameters (angle, gap, width) with controlled opacity. Use silhouette extraction and variable outlines to create depth.
how: Extend compose_lab.py to support layer-based grouping. Apply NPR shaders to layers with unique color palettes and stroke patterns for foreground emphasis.

title: Gradual Revelation Technique
text: Hide key story elements until climax, revealed through character perspective. Clues integrate subtly without explicit pauses - passed visually via background props that guide attention.
how: In storyboarding, plan a final reveal shot (e.g., deity's face through character's eyes for mythology videos). Background props (ancient artifacts, tech gadgets) as visual cues.

title: Dynamic Environmental Simulation
text: Add subtle wind effects using sine waves + noise for organic movement. Parameters: amplitude varies per element (0.03 for flowers, 0.09 for wild grass), frequency at 1.1-2.3Hz. Creates continuous life.
how: Implement GSAP wind effects in HyperFrames for trees, banners, or fabric elements. Apply sine waves with randomized offsets using JavaScript Math.sin().

title: Light-Sweep Reveal Canvas Shader Pass
text: Simulate a premium tech keynote light sweep using an offscreen canvas mask. Calculate length L along sweep angle normal: front = -soft + p * (L + soft * 2). Clip source via linear gradient mask with destination-in, and render a leading-edge highlight band (width band * 2) using 'lighter' composite mode at alpha 0.2-0.55 over the revealed pixels.
how: Implement in HyperFrames compose_lab.py to animate stat cards, tech feature unveils, or product shots upon voice hook triggers.

title: Per-Glyph Rolling Digit Scramble
text: Render high-energy kinetic numbers by giving each digit a staggered lock timestamp. Before lock time lk, substitute the digit with random characters sampled from '0123456789#%/*+=<>?$&@ABCDEFXZ' at 24fps with 3-tap vertical ghosting alpha [0.85, 0.3, 0.14]. At lk, snap into the true digit with a damped spring vertical bounce: dy = -px * 0.12 * exp(-d * 14) * cos(d * 40).
how: Add to compose_lab.py for stat counters and metric reveals in tech explainer reels.

title: Greedy Nearest-Slot Tile Flight Transition
text: Transition scattered elements into an organized grid by calculating Euclidean distances from all active items to target slots. Assign greedily using a sorted distance matrix. Animate each item along a curved quadratic Bezier arc with back(p, 1.35) elastic overshoot and rotational spring damping, morphing asset geometry into standardized grid tiles across 0.35s.
how: Implement in compose_lab.py for multi-asset summary cards, comparisons, and grid assemblies.
